data.exact_reserve_text: The prior year development is calculated from the 'Estimate of ultimate gross claims' development triangle on page 21, by comparing the 'Current estimate' for the 2022 underwriting year (32,716) to its estimate from 'One year later' (33,018), resulting in a release of 302 (thousands).
data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate reported a prior year reserve release of $0.302 million USD, calculated from the gross claims development triangle for the 2022 underwriting year. This represents a 0.65% release relative to the opening gross claims outstanding. No specific causal factors or named events for this movement were detailed in the report, though general factors like claims cost assumptions, market factors, and economic conditions are noted as influencing estimates. The gross premiums written for the year were $78.448 million USD, with the largest contributions from US Binders (27.57%) and Alternative Risks Binders (16.59%).
raw_causal_phrases: The principal assumption underlying the liability estimates is that the future claims development will follow a similar pattern to past claims development experience.
This includes assumptions in respect of average claim costs, claim handling costs, claim inflation factors and claim numbers for each underwriting year.

Additional qualitative judgements are used to assess the extent to which past trends may not apply in the future, for example: once-off occurrence; changes in market factors such as public attitude to claiming: economic conditions: as well as internal factors such as portfolio mix, policy conditions and claims handling procedures.
Judgement is further used to assess the extent to which external factors such as judicial decisions and government legislation affect the estimates.
Other key circumstances affecting the reliability of assumptions include variation in interest rates, delays in settlement and changes in foreign currency rates.

The uncertainty associated with the ultimate claims experience of an underwriting year is greatest when the underwriting year is at an early stage of development and the margin for future experience potentially being more adverse than assumed is at its highest.
data.data_quality_notes: The gross premium mix uses the 'class of business' breakdown from the Managing Agent's report on page 2, as no 'segmental analysis' note with standard regulatory classes was found. The prior year development is calculated from the gross claims development triangle, considering only the 2022 underwriting year as 'prior' (excluding 2023 and 2024 as per instructions). No specific named events or detailed causal factors for the prior year development were explicitly stated.
